name: Cwd Discipline
description: Enforces that agents stay in the user's current working directory by default, with explicit exceptions for notes, settings, mode-driven bindings, and user redirects.

enforceDiscipline.label: Enforce Discipline
enforceDiscipline.description: Master switch for the stay-in-cwd discipline. When on, agents refuse to operate on paths outside cwd unless one of the configured exceptions applies. When off, agents may freely read/write any path the OS permits. Off is rarely correct outside controlled environments.

allowedExceptionPaths.label: Allowed Exception Paths
allowedExceptionPaths.description: User-managed list of absolute paths or path patterns agents are permitted to access even when they sit outside cwd. Each entry is a path plus a one-line rationale. Add project-specific exceptions (e.g. a shared config dir, a downstream service repo); leave default seeds in place for the typical Obsidian/settings/script paths.

${SWT_SETTINGS_PATH}.value: Unified settings file at the SWT settings path

${SWT_SECRETS_PATH}.value: Read-only access to the secrets file (never logged or echoed)

${SWT_DIR}/scripts/**.value: Bundled SWT helper scripts (lprun-query, clipboard-read, etc.)

onRedirectMidSession.label: On Redirect Mid-Session
onRedirectMidSession.description: How TPM responds when the user verbally redirects the session to a different path mid-session (let's look at /other/path). accept treats the new path as in-scope for the remainder of the session without challenge. confirm prompts the user to confirm the redirect once before treating the path as in-scope. refuse blocks the redirect entirely and requires the user to disable cwd discipline. Default accept matches the existing universal posture.

treatModeBindingsAsExceptions.label: Treat Mode Bindings As Exceptions
treatModeBindingsAsExceptions.description: When on, an active session mode that binds the agent to a specific path (mode.cd binds to a project dir; mode.support binds per-app) implicitly extends cwd discipline to include the bound path. When off, mode bindings do not relax cwd discipline and the user must add each mode-bound path to Allowed Exception Paths manually. On is the typical default; off is for projects that want strict cwd-only.
